speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your sudden vertigo, can you describe the sensation—are you feeling like the room is spinning around you, or do you feel like you are losing your balance?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the spinning sensation return if you change your head position, such as rolling over in bed or looking up? Also, do you have any hearing loss or ringing in your ears?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or a feeling of fullness in the ear on the affected side? I also need to know if you have any accompanying neurological symptoms like double vision, slurred speech, or weakness in your limbs.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient is otherwise healthy with only a history of eczema. No prior episodes of similar nature. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the brief, position-triggered nature of your vertigo and lack of hearing symptoms, I suspect Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo. REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike maneuver

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: Positive, inducing nystagmus and reproducing patient’s symptoms of vertigo when head is turned to the left and laid back.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Positive, inducing nystagmus and reproducing patient’s symptoms of vertigo when head is turned to the left and laid back.

speaker: Doctor
text: The positive Dix-Hallpike maneuver confirms the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
